title: Bash Script Structure knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which topic is explicitly listed under “Bash Script Structure”?
questions.explanation: The supplied Bash.pdf curriculum lists “Shebangs and interpreter selection” under lesson 18, “Bash Script Structure”. Review the topic in the lesson content to connect the term with its practical use.

questions.prompt: Which approach is the strongest default when applying “Bash Script Structure”?
options: Skip version checks because all common environments provide the same Bash features.
Use quotes intentionally because Bash parses syntax and performs ordered expansions before execution.
Assume that a working happy-path example proves correctness for every input.
Evaluate constructed user-controlled strings as shell commands to reduce parsing code.
questions.answer_key: Use quotes intentionally because Bash parses syntax and performs ordered expansions before execution.
questions.explanation: Use quotes intentionally because Bash parses syntax and performs ordered expansions before execution. This approach keeps assumptions visible and makes results verifiable.

questions.prompt: Which practice best prevents a common reliability or maintenance error related to “Bash Script Structure”?
options: Use a small reproducible example, test an edge case, and record both the result and an important limitation.
Assume the command behaves the same across all versions and operating systems.
Skip invalid inputs because the example uses trusted sample data.
Treat one successful output as proof that the workflow is safe in production.
questions.answer_key: Use a small reproducible example, test an edge case, and record both the result and an important limitation.
questions.explanation: Use a small reproducible example, test an edge case, and record both the result and an important limitation. The appropriate checks depend on the target environment and should be reviewed before publishing a script.
